answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with quadratic staking. Each verified agent locks a bond in a shared ledger etched in quartz, and its voting weight is the square root of that bond. Hiding capital on a fake island yields far less influence than staking it once, so an attacker must lock capital proportional to the square of the power they seek. A slashing rule burns the bond of any double-voting agent, while a public beacon of attestations lets peers spot staked identities and ignore phantoms. A Sybil flood thus costs real, forfeitable capital, not free accounts.
